item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-08
item.description: Two instruments published nine days apart turned open-source work into something administrable: Zhejiang University's Taiyi 2.0 (released at Wuzhen 2026-11-04) aggregates commits, issues, merge requests and the process-and-results of human-AI collaboration into a verifiable capability profile usable for course credit, scholarship ranking and degree-output recognition, and signed a curriculum agreement with Huawei's CANN community on the formula 'universities organise the teaching, enterprises open the engineering scenarios, communities participate in guidance and evaluation'; and on 2026-11-06 Hangzhou Dianzi University project-launched a national group standard for the OPC (one-person-company) talent model, whose district draft already gated a real subsidy -- a nine-level ladder whose top three rungs are denominated in commercial orders, annual revenue and annual token consumption, with ¥150,000 per person in rent subsidy attached through Xihu District's F-class talent channel. Both sit inside OpenAtom's contribution-oriented talent-evaluation mechanism released at Tsinghua on 2025-04-18, where MIIT's vice-minister asked that open source be 'used' in talent evaluation. Measured against the demand side -- 100 recent commits on Ascend's PyTorch adapter, of which 51 carry @huawei.com and 16 @h-partners.com addresses, against 36 pull requests in the repository's entire history and none since 2026-10-01 -- the instruments describe a system building a supply of certified practitioners faster than any project has built a queue in which to receive them.
